Misc. No. 409/39
Sims
1st October, 39.
1

Two Japanese trucks conveying Japanese soldiers
turned back at Wuchan Road Bridge

At 10.25 a.m. 1/10/39, telephone message was
received from C.P.C. 2609 stating that Japanese trucks
had been held up by American Marines at Wuchan Road
Bridge.

Insp. i/c (Insp. Mason) D.S.I. Read and D.S.I.
Ting Hwa Keh immediately attended and on arrival found
the two trucks Lic. No.s 12 and 13 filled with Japanese
Soldiers were turning round and they drove back into
Chapel.

Enquiry from the American Marines revealed that
these two trucks had attempted to enter the Settlement.
On being held up by the American Marines, an English
speaking Japanese Officer spoke to the American Marines
and on it being explained to him that they were under
orders to prevent any such entry into their Sector the
Japanese Officer gave the necessary orders and after
turning round on the Settlement side of the Bridge,
both trucks drove back into Chapel.

The whole affair was orderly and nothing untoward
took place.

（批：加）
（批：SI (3/10) 8 1/10 Put 4/10 /Km）

在武定路桥被折返

1939年10月1日上午10时25分，接到
第2609号中央警亭电话报告，称日本卡车
在武定路桥被美国海军陆战队拦截。

主管督察（梅森 Mason 督察）、侦探副督察里德（Read）
和侦探副督察丁华克（Ting Hwa Keh）立即前往，
抵达时发现两辆车牌号为12和13、载满
日本士兵的卡车正在掉头，并驶回曹家渡。

向美国海军陆战队查询后得知，
这两辆卡车曾试图进入租界。
在被美国海军陆战队拦截后，一名会说英语的

该日本军官下达了必要命令，两辆卡车
在桥的租界一侧掉头后，驶回曹家渡。

整个事件秩序井然，未发生任何意外。

September 29, 1939.

MAINICHI

BRITISH SOLDIERS ENTER SHANGHAI CITY GOVERNMENT'S
SOCIAL OFFICE AND DEMAND WITHDRAWAL OF POLICE
GUARDS FROM ITS PREMISES

At 6.15 p.m. September 26 a
party of British soldiers entered the Social Bureau office
of the Shanghai City Government in the former Chinese
Chamber of Commerce on north Honan Road and attempted to
chase away two Chinese policemen who were on guard duty
there, informing them that the premises lie in the British
sector, but the British soldiers left the place when
the Chinese policemen refused to leave.
The premises in question are
situated in the Japanese sector, the British soldiers
having evacuated it as a result of an agreement reached
between Japanese and British military authorities.
Relative to the issue involved,
the Social Bureau of the Shanghai City Government states
that its office in the former Chamber of Commerce was
established after the outbreak of the local hostilities
and that the guards were placed there to protect the
office.
It would be an unpardonable crime
had the British soldiers insisted in their intentions.
After an investigation has been undertaken a strong protest
will be lodged with the British authorities.

25th. September, 39.
1.

ARREST OF U.S. MARINE BY S.C.S.P. BUREAU.

At 9.10p.m. September 24, 1939 Private A.
Hoeppen, F. Company, 2nd. Battalion and Private D.H.
Tener, D. Company, 1st. Battalion, U.S. Marines, came
to Bubbling Well Station and reported that Private H.C.
Helberg of D. Company, 1st. Battalion, had been arrest-
ed at 9p.m. on Yu Yuen Road by members of the S.C.S.P.
Bureau.

When questioned, the informants stated that
they had been in the Kirtel Garden, Yu Yuen Road
opposite to Jessfield Park main gate. They left this
cafe shortly before 9p.m. and walked Eastward along Yu
Yuen Road to the "Polo" Club at No. 147b. It was
their intention to enter but they could not do so
because one of them was in uniform and a notice posted
at the gate said that "men in uniform were not allowed"
Private Helberg became annoyed, pulled the notice from
the gate and tore it up. Wong Wing Woh (唐文玉), a
private watchman in uniform remonstrated in pidgin
English and Chinese with Helberg who responded by
knocking off the watchman's cap. A scuffle ensued
which was continued for about 100 yards farther east
along Yu Yuen Road, with Helberg's companions attempt-
ing to separate the men and get Helberg away.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 039）

美国海军陆战队士兵被上海特别市警察局逮捕。

1939年9月24日晚9时10分，美国海军陆战队第二营F连的 A. Hoeppen 列兵和第一营D连的 D.H. Tener 列兵来到静安寺分局报案，称第一营D连的 H.C. Helberg 列兵于晚9时在愚园路被上海特别市警察局成员逮捕。

经询问，报案人称他们此前一直在愚园路、静安公园正门对面的 Kirtel Garden（音译：柯特尔花园）。他们在晚9点前不久离开这家咖啡馆，沿愚园路向东步行至位于147b号的“Polo”俱乐部。他们本打算进入，但因其中一人身着军装，且门口张贴的告示写明“军人不得入内”，故未能进入。Helberg 列兵感到恼火，将告示从门上扯下并撕碎。身穿制服的私人保镖 Wong Wing Woh（唐文玉）用洋泾浜英语和中文与 Helberg 交涉，Helberg 则打掉了保镖的帽子。随后发生扭打，双方沿愚园路向东继续纠缠约100码，Helberg 的同伴试图将两人分开并将 Helberg 带走。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科 039）

At this point, the watchman blew his whistle
to attract Police attention, and a truck load of S.O.G.
P.M. men who were passing, stopped and took Private
Helberg into custody, these men, about 10 to 15 in
number, are said to have worked the bolts of their
rifles, and to have pointed their bayonets at the
Marine Party. The truck was driven west along Yu Yuen
Road and turned east onto Bremen Road.

The Officer of the day was informed of the
occurrence by Corporal Miller, U.S.M.C. Military Police
on behalf of D. I. Tabrum, and requested to attend the
station.

Lieutenant Hart, Assistant Intelligence Officer,
D.I. Tabrum and D. L. Hagerman proceeded to 92 Jessfield
Road and interviewed Mr. Kitaoka.

Both the watchman and Private Helberg were
brought to Mr. Kitaoka's office, and questioned, the
latter with the permission of Lieutenant Hart.

The watchman stated that after the marine had
torn up the notice, he attempted to pull him inside to
see the American manager. His reason for doing this
was to avoid being reprimanded for neglecting his duty.
In the scuffle which followed his cap was knocked off
and he received blows on the side of the head and nose
page_data.zh:

1/3.

此时，保镖吹响哨子以引起警方注意，一辆载有上海特别市警察局机动队（S.O.G. P.M.）人员的卡车路过并停下，将 Helberg 列兵拘捕。据说这些约有10至15人的警察拉动步枪枪栓，并用刺刀指向海军陆战队人员。卡车沿愚园路向西行驶，随后转入百老汇路（Bremen Road）向东行驶。

当日值班军官由美国海军陆战队宪兵 Miller 下士代表 Tabrum 侦探督察通知了此事，并被要求前往分局。

Hart 中尉（助理情报官）、Tabrum 侦探督察和 D. L. Hagerman 前往杰斯菲尔德路92号，会见了北冈先生（Mr. Kitaoka）。

保镖和 Helberg 列兵均被带到北冈先生的办公室接受询问，后者是在获得 Hart 中尉许可的情况下进行的。

保镖称，在该海军陆战队员撕毁告示后，他试图将其拉进去见美方经理。他这样做的原因是为了避免因失职而受到斥责。在随后的扭打中，他的帽子被打掉，头部侧面和鼻子遭到击打

U. S. Marine
Detained By
'Ta Tao' Men
An American Marine, member of
the 4th Regiment, was held for
almost two hours by the "Ta Tao"
police in the Western District of
Shanghai last night. He was de-
tained at 9 p.m. and released at
10.55 p.m.
The incident had its beginning in
front of the Welcome Cafe on Yu
Yuen Road near Jessfield Park.
While exact details were not avail-
able up to a late hour last night,
it is understood that the leather-
neck became involved in a verbal
argument and the watchman em-
ployed by the cafe blew his whistle.
About 20 "Ta Tao" policemen
answered the watchman's alarm
and the marine was overpowered
during the struggle that followed.
He is said to have been loaded in
a truck and taken away to a "Ta
Tao" police station in Jessfield.
Both the Shanghai Municipal
Police and the 4th Regiment
authorities were immediately notif-
ied and negotiations for the release
of the marine were started at once.
His release was affected after al-
most two hours of conversation.
As a result of this incident, the
United States naval and marine
authorities, fearing further affrays
of the same sort, immediately
placed the Yu Yuen Road district
out of bounds to leathernecks and
sailors. Marine and shore patrols
went through the area and order-
ed all naval men and marines to
leave.
As a result of this action,
cabarets, bars and bingo establish-
ments which line Yu Yuen Road
near Jessfield Park were almost
empty after 1 a.m.,

1939年9月25日
美国海军陆战队员
被“大道”警察
拘留
昨晚，在上海西区，一名隶属第四团的美军海军陆战队员被“大道”警察扣留了近两个小时。他于晚9时被拘留，于晚10时55分获释。
事件起因于静安公园附近愚园路上的 Welcome Cafe（音译：欢迎咖啡馆）门前。尽管直到昨晚很晚时候确切细节仍不清楚，但据悉这名“水兵”（leatherneck，海军陆战队俚语）卷入了一场口头争吵，咖啡馆雇佣的保镖吹响了哨子。
约20名“大道”警察响应保镖的警报，在随后的争斗中海军陆战队员被制服。据说他被装上一辆卡车，带往静安寺的一处“大道”警察局。
上海公共租界工部局警务处和第四团当局立即接到通知，并随即开始就释放该海军陆战队员进行谈判。经过近两个小时的交涉，他得以获释。
鉴于此次事件，美国海军和海军陆战队当局担心发生类似的进一步冲突，立即禁止海军陆战队员和水手进入愚园路地区。海军陆战队和岸上巡逻队穿过该区域，命令所有海军人员和海军陆战队员离开。
由于这一行动，凌晨1点后，静安公园附近愚园路两旁的歌舞厅、酒吧和宾果游戏场所几乎空无一人。

Subject. Minor Incident on Garden Bridge involving Italian Marines.
Made by. F.S. 240 Albon Forwarded by (签名)

Sir,

The undersigned respectfully begs to report that at 9.15 a.m. 1-5-39 four motor trucks loads of Italian Marines ( about 120 in all, armed with rifles. ) were observed going over Garden Bridge from South to North. On reaching the crown of the bridge they were stopped by the Japanese Naval N.C.O. and not allowed to proceed until the Japanese Naval N.C.O. had telephoned to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters for instructions.

The motor trucks were detained for from 3 to 5 minutes and then allowed to proceed to their destination, the Hongkew Rifle Range. It was subsequently ascertained that the Italian Marine Authorities had made previous arrangements with the Japanese Naval Landing Party to pass over the bridge but it appears that the Japanese Naval Sentries on the bridge had not received instructions and therefore knew nothing about the Italian Marines passing over until they telephoned their Headquarters for confirmation.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently.
(签名)

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. E. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 863/4/30
Date
APR 19 1939

Minor Incidents on
Garden Bridge

Three Japanese Civilians
Removed by Scots Sentry;
Consular Police Involved

Three incidents, all of a minor character it was stressed yesterday evening by police officials, occurred on Garden Bridge yesterday afternoon, members of the Seaforth Highlanders guard situated on the bridge being concerned in two of the incidents and a British civilian in the other one. Also involved were Japanese civilians and Consular Policemen.

The first incident occurred at 3.30 p.m. when a Seaforth sentry had trouble in attempting to remove three Japanese civilians from the vicinity of his box where they had been standing in spite of his orders to move on.

According to an eye-witness of the incident the three Japanese were behaving suspiciously round the box whereupon the sentry asked them to move on. They they did not do with the result that he went towards them and a struggle ensued during which an umbrella belonging to one of the men was broken at the stem.

With the assistance of a C.P.C. of the Shanghai Municipal Police and a Japanese sergeant the men eventually were removed from the vicinity by the sentry. Later the Japanese civilian whose umbrella had been broken lodged a complaint with the S.M.P. The fact was stressed that no interference was attempted by Japanese Consular policemen in the bridge or by the Japanese sentries.

Stopped by Highlander

While walking across the bridge on the west side at about 4.55 p.m. a British civilian named Fabian was seized by two Japanese policemen and marched across the road to the east side. No complaint was lodged by Mr. Fabian against this action, although the matter was reported to S.M.P. members on duty in the vicinity immediately after the occurrence.

In the third incident, which happened five minutes later, a Chinese coolie crossing the bridge from Hongkew, failed to stop at the Japanese sentry boxes and proceeded on his way to the Bund side. A Japanese Consular policeman immediately gave chase but was prevented from passing the Seaforth box by the sentry who stepped in his path and made him turn back. Meanwhile the coolie had run away.

It was not known last night whether any protests had been made regarding the incidents with the Japanese civilians and the Consular policemen, but it is believed that no such action will be taken by either of the parties concerned.

（批：19/4）

1939年4月19日

外白渡桥上的轻微事件

三名日本平民被苏格兰哨兵带离；
领事警察卷入其中

警方官员昨晚强调，昨天下午在外白渡桥发生了三起事件，均属轻微性质。海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）驻桥守卫人员参与了其中两起事件，另一名英国平民参与了另一起事件。涉事方还包括日本平民和领事警察。

第一起事件发生在下午3时30分，当时一名海福斯高地团哨兵在试图将三名日本平民从其岗亭附近带走时遇到麻烦，尽管他已命令他们离开，但这三人仍一直站在那里。

据该事件的目击者称，这三名日本人在岗亭周围行为可疑，于是哨兵要求他们离开。他们未予照办，导致哨兵走向他们，随后发生争执，期间其中一人的雨伞伞柄折断。

在上海公共租界警务处一名华捕巡长（C.P.C.）和一名日本军士的协助下，哨兵最终将这些男子从附近带离。后来，雨伞被毁的那名日本平民向工部局警务处提出投诉。值得强调的是，日本领事警察或日本哨兵均未试图干预桥上事务。

被高地团士兵拦下

下午4时55分左右，一名名叫法比安（Fabian）的英国平民在西侧过桥时，被两名日本警察抓住并强行带到路东一侧。法比安先生虽未就此行动提出投诉，但事发后立即向附近执勤的工部局警务处人员报告了此事。

第三起事件发生在五分钟后，一名从虹口方向过桥的中国苦力未在日本哨兵岗亭前停下，继续向外滩方向走去。一名日本领事警察立即追赶，但被海福斯高地团哨兵拦住，哨兵挡在其路径上并迫使其折返。与此同时，那名苦力已逃跑。

昨晚尚不清楚是否就涉及日本平民和领事警察的事件提出了任何抗议，但据信相关各方均不会采取此类行动。

（批注：19/4）
（批注：归档）

Made by P.S. 73 Blackley. Forwarded by (Signature)

Sir,

I beg to report that at 1.10 p.m. on the 5-4-39 I was
on duty at Garden Bridge when 4 soldiers of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party crossed the bridge from N. to S., on
reaching the British Military Sentry, Corporal (Captain crossed out) Cdr. Joll of
the Seaforth Highlanders who was Guard Commander, stopped
them and would not allow them to proceed, he then summoned the
Lance Corporal of the Guard while he went to telephone his
Headquarters, I proceeded to the scene and at this time a
Japanese Officer who was on duty on the Bridge also arrived
at the scene, J.P.C. 226 (Hongkew) acted as interpreter, it
appears that this party of Japanese soldiers wished to proceed
to a Japanese Junk on the Bund, they were armed with bayonets
and an Officer was in charge of them, which is the reason
why the Corporal (Captain crossed out) of the Guard stopped them.

The Japanese Officer finally gave the party an order to
proceed to their destination, and I asked the Lance Corporal
of the Guard if he was going to allow them to proceed and he
told me he could not stop them as they are not allowed to use
force. All this took place while the Guard Commander was
away telephoning to Headquarters. The name of the Lance
Corporal on Guard is Lance Corporal Paterson.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
T. Blackley.

states that he attempted to explain that he entered by

pistol and menaced him with it. The two Marines left
the restaurant and telephoned to the station.
D.S. Deaville and J.P.S. 134 accompanied by Private
Hill entered the restaurant and interviewed the manager-
ess. She stated that the Marines had not paid for the
sake they had consumed and that one of them had entered
a room occupied by Japanese customers and caused trouble
with them. D.S. Deaville and J.P.S. 134 entered this
room and found three Japanese citizens therein partaking
of food. Questioned by J.P.S. 134, they gave their
names as Kitaoka, Ozaki and Miyazaki, of the Japanese
Special Service Section, No. 92 Jessfield Road. They
denied menacing the Marine with a pistol.
At 10.00p.m. above date, Major Monahan, U.S.M.C.,
and a party of Marines arrived.
Major Monahan, after questioning Privates Hill and
Ray, requested the S.M.Police to search the Japanese.
D.S. Deaville instructed J.P.C. 143 to do the searching
and he refused stating that the S.M.Police had no
authority to search a Japanese subject. One of the
Japanese then came forward and requested J.P.C. 143 to
search him. The J.P.C. searched him in a half hearted
way.

侦探长 Deaville 和日本警员（J.P.S.）134号在希尔二等兵的陪同下进入餐厅并采访了女经理。她声称海军陆战队队员未支付所饮清酒的费用，且其中一人进入了有日本顾客的房间并与他们制造了麻烦。侦探长 Deaville 和日本警员（J.P.S.）134号进入该房间，发现三名日本公民正在那里用餐。经日本警员（J.P.S.）134号询问，他们自报姓名为北冈（Kitaoka）、尾崎（Ozaki）和宫崎（Miyazaki），隶属于极司菲尔路92号日本特务机关。他们否认用手枪威胁海军陆战队队员。
在上述日期的晚上10点，美国海军陆战队莫纳汉（Monahan）少校及一队海军陆战队队员到达。
莫纳汉少校在询问希尔和雷二等兵后，要求工部局警务处搜查日本人。侦探长 Deaville 指示日本警员（J.P.C.）143号进行搜查，但他拒绝了，声称工部局警务处无权搜查日本臣民。随后一名日本人走上前，要求日本警员（J.P.C.）143号搜查他。该日本警员敷衍了事地进行了搜查。

SHANGHAI TIMES,

OCT 15 1938

SEAFORTHS HELD UP
Shortly after 2 o'clock yesterday
afternoon, a number of Seaforth
Highlanders proceeding across the
Garden Bridge in a motor truck
were held up by the Japanese sen-
tries on duty. The driver of the
vehicle was said to have been asked
for a pass and informed the sentry
that it was not customary to carry
one. The matter was settled after
some discussion, and the Seaforths
were allowed to proceed.

1938年10月15日

海福斯高地团受阻
昨天下午2点后不久，一批乘坐卡车经过外白渡桥的海福斯高地团士兵被执勤的日本哨兵拦下。据说司机被要求出示通行证，并告知哨兵携带通行证并非惯例。经过一番讨论后，此事得以解决，海福斯高地团士兵获准通行。

Data Oct. 13th. 1938.

REPORT

Subject (in full) British Military Vehicles stopped by Japanese Sentry on
the Garden Bridge.

Made by F. S. 76 Aksenoff Forwarded by (签名)

Sir,

I beg to report that I was on duty today (Garden Bridge
7 a.m. to 3 p.m.). At about 10.10 a.m. a British Military
truck Lic. No. S D F 153, driven by a soldier and carrying
another soldier as a passenger, was proceeding from South to
North over the Garden Bridge and was stopped by Japanese Sentry
on the North side of the Bridge.

A Corporal in charge of Seaforths' Guard on the Bridge ask-
ed me to go over and find out why the truck was stopped. I
went and was told by the driver of the truck that Japanese asked
them where they were going to. When explained the British sold-
iers were told to wait whilst the Japanese rang up to their Head-
quarters.

At 10.15 a.m. a British Military M/Car Lic. No. S D F 178
driven by a soldier and carrying as passengers three British
Military officers and proceeding in the same direction, was also
stopped and told to wait behind the truck. At 10.20 a.m. both
vehicles were allowed to proceed.

D. O. "A"
D. C. (Special Branch)

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
F. S. Aksenoff

Shanghai Power Co. 2800 Y'poo Road to the effect that three
male Japanese in military uniform had been arrested in the above
company's compound and that he, 1st Lieutenant, Platt wished to
hand the Japanese over to the S.M.P. The undersigned accompanied
by S.I. MacLeod and J.P.C. 11 proceeded to the above address and
ascertained the following:- At about 8.05 p.m. 16/9/38
Russian and Chinese watchmen employed at the Power Station
observed three Japanese in uniform walking about the compound
near the river, the watchmen immediately informed the U.S.
Marines and foreign employees resulting in the U.S. Marines
arresting the Japanese and subsequently informing this station.
The three Japanese when questioned gave their names as follows,
I. Sano, K. Sakagami and M. Iwaki and stating that they were
employed by and attached to the Japanese Military to navigate
small motor vessels on the Whangpoo River and further that

inadvertently alighted in the compound of the Power Company.
The three men appeared to have been drinking and it is thought
by the undersigned that on finding the approach to jetties
closed by barbed wire they had entered the compound hoping to
find their way out to the roadway. Japanese Military Police
were informed and a Military Police Sergeant Major and a

1938年9月16日晚上8时17分，接到驻杨树浦路2800号上海电力公司的美军陆战队负责人 W.N. 普拉特 (W.N. Platt) 中尉的电话留言，称三名身穿军服的日本男子在上述公司院内被捕，普拉特中尉希望将日本人移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处 (S.M.P.)。具名人与巡长麦克劳德 (MacLeod) 及警员编号11一同前往上述地址，查明情况如下：- 1938年9月16日晚上约8时05分，发电厂雇用的俄国和中国更夫观察到三名身穿制服的日本人在河边附近的院内走动，更夫立即通知了美军陆战队和外籍员工，导致美军陆战队逮捕了这些日本人，随后通知本捕房。
经讯问，这三名日本人自报姓名分别为 I. 佐野 (Sano)、K. 坂上 (Sakagami) 和 M. 岩木 (Iwaki)，并称他们受雇于日本军方，附属于日本军队，负责在黄浦江上驾驶小型摩托艇，此外他们还驻扎在点岛 (Point Island) 的旧鱼市场。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

SEP 1 4 1938

Action of Japanese
Held “Aggressive”

A vigorous protest was addressed yesterday by Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett, commanding the British Forces in the Shanghai area, to the Rear-Admiral in command of the Japanese Naval Landing Party over the arrest, on Monday afternoon, of a British soldier for alleged trespass over the boundary at Blockhouse “B” near Shanghai’s celebrated “Windy Corner.” The soldier, Private Mac-Kenzie, of the First Battalion the Seaforth Highlanders, was seized by Japanese sentries while he was engaged in wiring work near the block-house.

It is understood that the protest filed by Major-General Smollett yesterday emphasized that the action of the Japanese was considered both “un-friendly” and “aggressive.”

1938年9月14日

日军行动
被指“具有侵略性”

上海地区英军司令 A. P. D. 特尔弗-斯莫利特 (A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett) 少将于昨日向日本海军陆战队指挥官海军少将提出强烈抗议，抗议内容是关于周一下午一名英国士兵因涉嫌在上海著名的“风角” (Windy Corner) 附近的“B”号碉堡处越界而被捕一事。这名士兵是西福斯高地团第一营的麦肯齐 (Mac-Kenzie) 列兵，当时他正在碉堡附近进行布线作业，被日本哨兵抓获。

据悉，斯莫利特少将昨日提交的抗议书强调，日方的行动被认为既“不友好”又“具有侵略性”。

经具名人查询，查明情况如下：-

晚上约7时20分，一辆牌照号不详的 X/卡车正由北向南驶过外白渡桥，在桥顶被日本哨兵和宪兵拦截，以便检查司机的通行证和货物。在桥顶停留几秒后，日本宪兵显然指示 X/卡车司机向前开几码，等待检查。

1/第2页。

英方卫队负责士官注意到卡车阻碍了他的哨兵，便告诉卡车司机（一名中国人）驾车离开哨兵区域，卡车随即沿外滩向南驶离。

隶属虹口捕房的警员编号60韦特 (Waite) 走近麦克弗森 (McPherson) 列兵哨位，询问他为何命令 N/卡车移动。

随后，弗莱彻下士告知警员编号60远离哨兵，因为不允许与英国哨兵交谈。（警员编号60报告称，当他试图接近哨兵时，下士推开了他，但弗莱彻下士予以否认，并称他是站在警员编号60面前，阻挡其接近哨兵）。

此时，几名日本士兵和宪兵从桥顶走过来，到达距英国哨兵岗亭仅几英尺的地方，显然是为了要求解释，弗莱彻下士立即从英国驻华领事馆 grounds 调出卫队，结果日本军方人员撤退并返回桥上的岗位。

日本高级军官立即被召至现场，随后隶属西福斯高地团的马歇尔 (Marshall) 中尉抵达，在该事件向他

SEP 6 1938

Seaforths Comply with
Japanese Request

British Sentry Boxes
Moved Nearer Bund

The sight of a party of Seaforth
Highlanders marching along Garden
Bridge at about 5 p.m. yesterday
afternoon gave rise to rumours that
a further incident had developed
over the question of the situation of
the British and Japanese sentry boxes
in the centre of the bridge, but a
"North-China Daily News" repre-
sentative, who visited the scene
shortly afterwards, was informed
that nothing untoward had occurred.
Shortly before 5 p.m., he was
told, the Seaforths moved their
sentry boxes into the road in order
to bring them in line with those
occupied by the Japanese sentries.
A Japanese officer, who witnessed
the removal of the boxes from the
pavement into the road, then came
forward and asked the Guard Com-
mander if it would be possible to
take the boxes about twenty metres
along the bridge towards the Bund
in order to facilitate the work of
searching cars and avoiding traffic
congestion on the road.
Stating that he would have to
inform an officer of the request, the
Lance-Corporal in charge of the
guard telephoned to the British
military headquarters and the Brigade
Major visited the scene, where he
conferred with the Japanese officer.
All the conversation was carried
on amicably, the reporter was
informed, and the Brigade Major
agreed to comply with the Japanese
request. The rest of the Seaforth
guard were then sent for to remove
the boxes, which they carried lower
down the bridge. Having finished
this task, they marched back to their
quarters at the H.M. Consulate, and
at no time, it was stated, was there
any evidence, of bad feeling between
the British and Japanese.

1938年9月6日

西福斯团遵从
日军要求

英国哨兵岗亭
移近外滩

昨天下午5点左右，一队西福斯高地团士兵沿外白渡桥行进，这一景象引发了谣言，称因桥中央英日哨兵岗亭的位置问题又发生了新的事件，但《字林西报》的一名代表随后访问现场，获悉并未发生任何异常事件。
据告知，在下午5点前不久，西福斯团将他们的哨兵岗亭移入车道，使其与日本哨兵占据的岗亭排成一线。一名目睹岗亭从人行道移至车道的日本军官随即上前，询问卫队指挥官是否可以将岗亭沿桥向外滩方向移动约二十米，以便于搜查车辆并避免道路交通拥堵。
负责卫队的下士表示需向上级军官汇报此请求，遂致电英军总部，旅参谋长亲临现场，与日本军官进行了磋商。据记者获悉，所有谈话均在友好气氛中进行，旅参谋长同意遵从日方的要求。随后，其余西福斯卫队成员被召来移除岗亭，他们将岗亭搬至桥的下游位置。完成这项任务后，他们列队返回英国领事馆的营房，据称，在此期间，英日双方没有任何不和的迹象。

Sir,

The undersigned begs to report when on duty at the Garden
Bridge at 5.25 p.m. 3-9-38, Captain Nesson of the Seaforth when
visiting the Garden Bridge Sentries observed a Japanese Sentry
standing on the West side of the bridge four yards south of his
(the Japanese) sentry box. The said sentry box is situated three
yards south of the centre line of the crown of the bridge.

According to the British sentries orders, they must walk
20 yds north and 20 yards south of their own box and it was found
that the Japanese Sentry was standing on the British sentry's beat
Captain Nesson (through an interpreter) requested the Japanese
officer to remove his sentry furth North and in line with his
own box. The Japanese officer objected and explained that his
sentry was necessary on the south side of the bridge to control
the north bound traffic.

Captain Nesson again explained his reasons and requested
the Japanese officer to move his sentry and later the matter
could be settled between their respective Headquarters. An
agreement was reached and the sentry moved as requested after
measurements of the positions had been taken by the Japanese
military.

I am, Sir,

具名人谨此报告，1938年9月3日下午5时25分，本人在外白渡桥当值时，西福斯团的内森 (Nesson) 上尉在视察外白渡桥哨兵时，发现一名日本哨兵站在其（日本）岗亭以南四码处的桥西侧。该岗亭位于桥顶中心线以南三码处。

根据英国哨兵的命令，他们必须在自己的岗亭以北20码和以南20码范围内巡逻，经查发现，该日本哨兵正站在英国哨兵的巡逻区内。内森上尉（通过翻译）要求日本军官将其哨兵向北移动，与其岗亭对齐。日本军官提出异议，并解释说，他的哨兵必须站在桥的南侧以控制北向交通。

内森上尉再次解释其原因，并要求日本军官移动其哨兵，随后此事可由各自总部解决。双方达成协议，在日本军方测量了位置后，哨兵按要求进行了移动。

page_data.en:
Excitement On Garden Bridge
British, Nippon Sentries Stage
Verbal Battle Over Boundary

Japanese bluejackets and Sea-forth Highlanders had a bit of excitement among themselves on Garden Bridge yesterday afternoon. The imaginary boundary line that bisects the center of the bridge in these troublesome days was the cause of the arguments.
Under ordinary circumstances, Japanese sentries stand on one side of the line while the Seaforths on duty on top of the bridge stand on the south side of the boundary.
When a Seaforth corporal took up duty on the bridge at 4.30 p.m. yesterday, he found a bluejacket on the south side of the line. Or so it was alleged.
The corporal objected and insisted that the Japanese move back across the line. The bluejacket had other ideas on the subject and insisted upon remaining where he was. More Seaforths put in their appearance. So did more Japanese bluejackets.
After the discussion had been underway for some time, an officer of the Seaforth Highlanders arrived on the bridge and investigated. A Japanese interpreter also was called to the scene.
More words followed and at precisely 5.15 p.m., just 30 minutes after the argument started, the Japanese bluejacket returned to his own side of the line. The matter was settled peacefully, everybody smiled and duty was resumed as usual.
page_data.zh:
外白渡桥上的骚动
英日哨兵就边界问题发生口角

昨日下午，日本水兵与海福斯高地团（Seaforth Highlanders）士兵在外白渡桥上发生了一点小摩擦。在这动荡的时期，那条将桥面中心一分为二的假想界线成为了争论的起因。
在通常情况下，日本哨兵站在界线的一侧，而在桥上执勤的海福斯高地团士兵则站在界线的南侧。
据称，昨日下午4时30分，一名海福斯高地团下士上桥执勤时，发现一名日本水兵站在界线的南侧。
该下士提出抗议，坚持要求日本人退回到界线另一侧。那名水兵对此另有看法，坚持留在原地。更多的海福斯高地团士兵出现。更多的日本水兵也出现了。
经过一段时间的争论后，一名海福斯高地团军官来到桥上进行调查。一名日语翻译也被召至现场。
双方又争执了一番，就在下午5时15分整，即争论开始后整整30分钟，那名日本水兵回到了界线己方一侧。此事和平解决，众人相视一笑，照常恢复执勤。

MALE CHINESE ARRESTED IN BRITISH MILITARY SECTOR BY
JAPANESE SENTRY ATTEMPTING TO CRAWL THROUGH BARBED WIRE.

At 1.50p.m. 10/8/38, a male Chinese crawled through
the barbed wire onto Keswick Road near Tunsin Road. A
Japanese sentry caught sight of him and gave chase by
riding a bicycle over St. Western Road barrier, arresting
him on Keswick Road.

The Japanese soldier attempted to take the man back
across the railway, but was prevented from doing so by
British Military on duty there, who took the man to
Brenan Road Post.

British Military informed Bubbling Well Station, and
the man was handed over to this Station for interrogation.
He stated:-
His name is Ting Kwan Doe (丁關多), 25, Shanghai,
S/collie, living at 67 Fah Wah Village off St. Western
Road.

He gave the following story:-
At about 8a.m. 10/8/38 he went to visit his mother
Ting Jae Sa (丁齋氏), living at 30 San Ching Hsien off
Brenan Road, west of the railway line. Not being in
possession of a Japanese pass, he crawled through the
wire, and was successful in reaching his mother's house,
where he gave her $4.00 which he had brought for her.
He was on his way back to Fah Wah Village when he
was arrested by the Japanese sentry.

一名中国男子在日本哨兵试图爬过铁丝网时，于英军防区被捕。

1938年8月10日下午1时50分，一名中国男子爬过铁丝网，进入靠近同新路的凯斯威克路（Keswick Road，今新闸路附近）。一名日本哨兵发现了他，骑自行车越过圣西路（St. Western Road，今西摩路/陕西北路一带）路障进行追赶，并在凯斯威克路将其逮捕。

这名日本士兵试图将该男子带回铁路另一侧，但被在那里执勤的英军阻止，英军将该男子带至布伦南路（Brenan Road，今山海关路）岗哨。

英军通知了静安寺路分局，该男子被移交给本分局进行审讯。他陈述如下：
姓名：丁关多（Ting Kwan Doe），25岁，上海人，职业为苏格兰牧羊犬饲养员（S/collie，原文如此，可能指狗贩或相关职业），住在圣西路法华村67号。

他讲述了以下经过：
1938年8月10日上午8点左右，他去探望住在铁路线西侧、布伦南路三庆里30号的母亲丁斋氏（Ting Jae Sa）。由于没有日本通行证，他爬过铁丝网，成功到达母亲家，并将带来的4美元交给了她。他在返回法华村的途中被日本哨兵逮捕。

With the assistance of the Japanese authorities, a
visit was paid to San Ching Mian, and the mother of Ting
Kwan Dec was located. When questioned, she said that her
son Ting Kwan Doe lived with her. At about 2p.m., 16/8/38
he left home with the intention of visiting his sister
Lee Ting Sz(李丁氏) at 97 Fah Wah Village to borrow
$4.00.

Further questioned, Ting Kwan Dec reversed his
former statement and stated that he was arrested by a
Japanese soldier on a bicycle after he had passed through
the barbed wire on Keswick Road while on the way to his
sister's home. He added that his first statement was
incorrect due to fright.

He stated that both his mother's and his name are
registered with the Japanese authorities as residents in
San Ching Mian, and that no Military pass for travelling
had been issued to them.

As a request has been made by the Japanese Authorit-
ies for this man to be handed over to them, he has been
detained. His finger prints show no previous record, and
he will be detained pending further instructions from
Headquarters.

在日本当局的协助下，警方前往三庆里（San Ching Mian），找到了丁关多（原文误作 Ting Kwan Dec）的母亲。经询问，她说儿子丁关多（Ting Kwan Doe）与她同住。1938年8月16日下午2点左右，他离家打算去法华村97号看望姐姐李丁氏（Lee Ting Sz），并借款4美元。

经进一步讯问，丁关多（原文误作 Ting Kwan Dec）推翻了之前的供词，称他在前往姐姐家的途中，在凯斯威克路爬过铁丝网后，被一名骑自行车的日本士兵逮捕。他补充说，之前的供词因受惊吓而不实。

他表示，他和母亲的名字都在日本当局登记为三庆里的居民，但他们并未获发任何军事通行证件。

由于日本当局要求移交此人，他已被拘留。其指纹显示无前科，他将等待总部进一步指示期间继续被拘留。

Sir,
At 1.20 p.m. on the 9.6.38., C.P.C. 2803 reported
to the station through street telephone Box No. 10 Ichang Rd
Bridge, that 2 Japanese Marines were laying telephone wires
from Ichang Road Bridge to the N.W.K. No. 3 and 4 Mills No. 19

section attended the station and stated that no permission had
been given the Japanese Authorities to lay these wires and

on and after a heated argument with the Japanese Authorities,

May 3rd, 38.

Report on Japanese Military guard at the Garden Bridge attempting
to detain a truck hired by the British Naval Authorities.

Det. Insp. A. Telfer

Sir,

About 8.25a.m. on May 3rd 1938 Sub Inspector Moore, on
Charge Room duty, telephoned the undersigned and stated there
was trouble outside the British Consulate between the Japanese
Military and the Seaforth Highlander's guard in connection with
a truck which had just come over the Garden Bridge.

D.S.I. Ovsiannikoff and the undersigned proceeded to the
location stated, but on arrival discovered that the disturbance
had settled and the Sergeant in charge of the Seaforth Highlanders
guard was dismissing the men he had called out.

From enquiries made on the scene by the undersigned the
following was ascertained:-

About 8.10a.m. on May 3rd 1938 a motor truck,
International Settlement License No. 16639, French
Concession Licence No. 1357, flying a Union Jack flag
attached to the side of the wind screen in front
of the drivers seat (right hand drive), driven by
a Chinese chauffeur accompanied by Able Seaman
Burgess of the H.M.S. "Aphis", was crossing
the Garden Bridge conveying stores from the
Eastern District to The French Bund for the
British Naval Authorities. Whilst the truck
was crossing it was stopped near the crown of
the bridge by the Japanese Military guard and
Municipal Police, and Able Seaman Burgess was
asked for a pass. He informed those who
inquired, who he was and what he was transporting
at the same time he gave the Japanese Warrant
Officer the consignment order. As far as could

关于日本军队卫兵在外白渡桥试图扣留英国海军当局租用卡车的报告。

侦探督察 A. Telfer

先生，

1938年5月3日上午8时25分左右，负责接待室工作的摩尔（Moore）副督察打电话给本人，称在英国领事馆外，日本军队与海福斯高地团卫兵之间因一辆刚驶过外白渡桥的卡车而发生纠纷。

特别调查员奥夫相尼科夫（Ovsiannikoff）和本人前往所述地点，但到达时发现骚乱已平息，负责海福斯高地团卫兵的警长正在解散他召集的人员。

经本人在现场查询，查明情况如下：

1938年5月3日上午8时10分左右，一辆机动车卡车，国际租界牌照号16639，法租界牌照号1357，在驾驶员座位前方挡风玻璃侧面悬挂着一面英国国旗（右舵驾驶），由中国司机驾驶，陪同人员为 HMS “Aphis” 号舰上的二等水兵伯吉斯（Burgess），正代表英国海军当局将物资从东区运往法外滩。当卡车过桥时，在桥顶附近被日本军队卫兵和巡捕拦下，并要求二等水兵伯吉斯出示通行证。他向询问者表明了自己的身份和所运输的物品，同时向日本准尉出示了货运单。据查

be ascertained the British Naval Authorities
have arranged with the Japanese Military
Authorities a permanent pass for vehicles
conveying their property over the Garden Bridge.
However, when the truck commenced to continue its
way South over the bridge the Japanese Warrant
Officer kept on the running board apparently with
the intention that the truck should turn back,
but the chauffeur continued on and turned round
at the South end of the bridge and parked the
truck on the North side of the main entrance to
the British Consulate facing West on Soochow Road.
By this time other four Japanese soldiers, who
apparently had been shouting after the moving
truck, came and posted themselves round it.
Sub. Insp. Hale who arrived on the scene and
on ascertaining the facts of the circumstances
then asked J.P.S. 76 to inform the Japanese Military
about the truck and who it was being utilised by.
He did so then informed Sub. Inspector Hale that the
Japanese officer wanted the truck to go back over
the bridge for the goods on it to be examined and
the matter of the pass gone into. Sub. Inspector
Hale then spoke to Sergeant MacLellan in charge of
the Seaforth Highlander's British Consulate guard
and agreed that the truck should remain where it
was until instructions were received from a senior
military or naval officer. J.P.S. 76 was then
informed by Sub. Inspector Hale to explain to the
page_data.zh:

明，英国海军当局已与日本军方当局就车辆经外白渡桥运送其财产事宜安排了永久通行证。然而，当卡车开始继续向南过桥时，日本准尉一直站在踏板上，显然是想让卡车掉头，但司机继续前行，在桥南端转弯，将卡车停在英国领事馆主入口北侧，面向西苏州路。此时，另外四名日本士兵赶来，他们此前似乎一直在对着移动的卡车喊叫，并围在卡车周围。随后赶到现场的哈尔（Hale）副督察在查明情况后，请日本巡捕76号通知日本军方有关卡车及其使用者的情况。他照办后告知哈尔副督察，日本军官要求卡车退回桥上，以便检查货物并核查通行证事宜。哈尔副督察随后与负责英国领事馆守卫的海福斯高地团麦克莱伦（MacLellan）警长交谈，并同意卡车应留在原地，直到收到高级军事或海军军官的指示。随后，哈尔副督察指示日本巡捕76号向

page_data.en:

Japanese senior officer the decision come to.
By this time Able Seaman Burgess proceeded
inside the British Consulate to try and locate
an officer, but was unsuccessful. Sub. Inspector
Hale then reported what had occurred to the Central
Police Station.
Another lorry containing British Naval
ratings arrived and on then noticing something
peculiar had happened, stopped. Petty Officer
Fisher in charge of the squad then came across to
where the truck was when Sub. Inspector Hale
explained to him what had occurred. He immediately
took the seat in the truck vacated by the Japanese
Officer, who had been trying to start it, and told
the Chinese chauffeur to drive on. Sub. Inspector
Hale then interpreted to the Chinese chauffeur, who
immediately started the vehicle. He drove it round
the traffic post nearby the British Consulate then
went South along the New Bund. The Japanese
military nearby, who thought the truck was
returning over the Garden Bridge were astounded when
they saw the direction it took and gave chase, but
were outdistanced. The Japanese senior officer then
returned to Sergeant McLellan in charge of the
Seaforth Highlander's guard, and tried to force him
to accompany them over the Garden Bridge by catching
him by the arm. He also attempted to force Sub
page_data.zh:

日本高级军官解释已做出的决定。
此时，二等水兵伯吉斯进入英国领事馆试图寻找一名军官，但未成功。哈尔副督察随后向中央巡捕房报告了发生的情况。
另一辆载有英国海军士兵的卡车到达，注意到发生了异常情况后停下。负责小队的费舍尔（Fisher） Petty Officer（海军士官）随即走到卡车所在处，哈尔副督察向他解释了发生的情况。他立即坐进日本军官刚才试图启动卡车而离开的座位，并命令中国司机开车。哈尔副督察随即向中国司机翻译，司机立即启动车辆。他驾车绕过英国领事馆附近的交通岗，然后沿新外滩向南行驶。附近的日本军人原以为卡车要返回外白渡桥，看到其行驶方向后大吃一惊并进行追赶，但未能追上。随后，日本高级军官回到负责海福斯高地团卫兵的麦克莱伦警长处，抓住他的手臂，试图强迫他陪同他们过外白渡桥。他还试图强迫副

page_data.en:
Inspector Hale likewise".
Sergeant McLellan on realising what the Japanese Officer
meant immediately rang a bell at the main entrance of the
British Consulate gate, which turned out the guard( three
in number) who came with fixed bayonets. The sergeant also
fixed his bayonet then lined the guard in front of the
Consulate gate. He then motioned to the Japanese Military
to go over the bridge, and they realising the warning
immediately returned to their posts.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Alexander Weir
Det. Inspector.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Sub/Inspector Hale
native of England taken by me Self
at Central Stn. on the 3-5-38 and interpreted by

At about 8.10 a.m. 3-5-38, whilst on duty at the centre
of Garden Bridge, C.P.C. 1142 came up and informed me that
British and Japanese Military were involved in an altercation
outside the gateway of H.B.M's. Consulate-General. I proceeded
thence immediately and found M/Truck Licence No. F. 1357, driven
by a Chinese and flying the Union Jack in front ranked at the
kerb. Able Seaman Burgess of H.M.S. "Aphis" was standing nearby
and with him were Sgt. MacLellan, Seaforth Highlanders, in charge
of the Consulate Guard, J.P.S. 76 (Hongkew) and a Sub-Lieutenant
of the Japanese Army (one gold strip and one gold star on
epaulettes) wearing the brassard of the Military Police. I asked
what was the matter and Burgess explained that he was in charge
of the lorry which was conveying stores from the Eastern District
to the French Bund and that whilst crossing Garden Bridge the
Japanese Military and Municipal Police had approached and asked
for a pass. He told them who he was and what he was transporting
and gave the officer the consignment order. He added that the
British Naval Authorities had arranged a permanent Pass for
vehicles conveying their property over the bridge. The vehicle
meanwhile was proceeding slowly in a line of traffic and after
going a little further Burgess heard shouting and saw he was being
pursued so swung around and pulled up outside the Consulate.
At the conclusion of this talk I asked J.P.S. 76 to translate it
to the Japanese Officer. He did so and then turned to me and
said that the officer wanted the lorry to go back over the
bridge for the goods to be examined and the matter of the pass
gone into. Whilst this was going on four privates of the

以下系由我本人在中央捕房于1938年5月3日对出生于英格兰的黑尔副巡官进行的问话笔录，并由

1938年5月3日上午8时10分左右，当本人在外白渡桥中心执勤时，华捕1142号上前告知我，英军与日军在英国驻华总领事馆大门外发生争执。我随即前往现场，发现一辆牌照号为 F. 1357 的机动卡车停在路边，由一名中国人驾驶，车前悬挂英国国旗。“阿菲斯”号（H.M.S. "Aphis"）皇家海军上等水兵伯吉斯站在附近，与他在一起的还有负责领事馆警卫的西福斯高地团麦克莱伦警士、虹口捕房日籍警员76号，以及一名佩戴宪兵臂章的日本陆军少尉（肩章上有一条金杠和一颗金星）。我询问发生了何事，伯吉斯解释说，他负责驾驶这辆从东区向法租界外滩运送物资的卡车，在经过外白渡桥时，日军和工部局警察上前要求出示通行证。他向他们表明了自己的身份及所运货物，并将发货单交给该军官。他补充说，英国海军当局已为运送其财产过桥的车辆安排了永久通行证。与此同时，该车辆正缓慢地在车流中行进，又前行了一小段距离后，伯吉斯听到喊叫声，发现自己被追赶，于是掉头并在领事馆外停下。谈话结束后，我请日籍警员76号将此情况翻译给日本军官。他照做了，然后转向我说，该军官要求卡车退回桥上，以便检查货物并核查通行证事宜。在此期间，四名

Japanese Army armed with rifles had arrived and posted themselves round the lorry. I then spoke to Sgt. Maclellan and we agreed that the lorry should remain until instructions were received from the first available officer. I told J.P.S. 76 of this and asked him to tell the officer and also asked Burgess to try to locate an officer in the Senior Naval Officer's offices in the Consulate compound. I then reported to the Station (S.I.Hours on duty).. Another lorry conveying British Naval ratings next arrived, and seeing something amiss, Petty Officer Fisher, in charge, stepped and came across. I told him what had happened so he took the seat vacated by the Japanese officer, who had been trying to start the vehicle, and told the chauffeur to drive on. I interpreted this to the latter, telling him to "Khe, khe". The vehicle moved forward and swung round South into the New Bund. The Japanese, apparently thinking it was going back North over the bridge where they wanted it were taken aback for a moment and then gave chase but were outdistanced. The officer then came back and caught Sgt. Maclellan by the arm and tried to force him to accompany him over the bridge. He then transferred his attentions to me in an attempt to do the same whereupon Sgt. Maclellan turned out the guard and the Japanese retired over the bridge. The incident was witnessed, in part by Sub-Inspector Furness (Hongkew), to whom I had got word at the outset, and by B.S.Thompson who arrived from Central Station.

The following is the statement of F. S. 38 R. Thompson.
native of....................................................taken by me.......................
at Central Station on the 3-5-38 ............and interpreted by Self.

Sir,
    The undersigned begs to report. At 8.20 a.m., 3-5-38
S. I. Moore, Officer on Charge Room duty, told me to proceed
to the Garden Bridge. On arrival, I saw m/truck Settlement
Licence 16639 and F. 1317 outside the British Consulate gates
surrounded by four Japanese Soldiers, and two Privates and one
sergeant of the British Consulate guard. At 8.25 a.m., a
m/truck with 5 British Naval ratings crossed the Garden Bridge
and stopped to make enquiries. It was then decided that the
detained m/truck should continue on its journey. J.P.S. 76
ordered the Chinese chauffeur to leave the driving seat, the
order was disregarded and the m/truck was driven off with the
3 Japanese Soldiers in pursuit.
    A few moment later the soldiers returned, the senior
soldier took hold of the British Guard Commander's sleeve and
motioned him to proceed with him over the Garden Bridge, at
the same time 3 more Japanese Soldiers ran from the Garden
Bridge towards the British Consulate.
    The British Guard Commander pulled his sleeve from the
Japanese Soldier's grip, entered the sentry box and pressed
the alarm bell, immediately 3 soldiers of the Consulate Guard
turned out with fixed bayonets, the Sergeant fixed his bayonet,
lined the guard in front of the Consulate gate and motioned
with his rifle to the Japanese Soldiers. The Japanese under-
stood the warning and immediately retreated to the centre of
the road, a few words was passed between them and they then
proceeded North over the Garden Bridge. The footpath in the
vicinity of the Consulate gates was cleared of the remainder
of the Japanese civilians.
                                        I am, Sir, Your Obedient Servant,
                                        R. Thompson
                                        F. S. 38

先生，
    卑职谨此报告。1938年5月3日上午8时20分，
    值班室警官 S. I. 穆尔命我前往外白渡桥。抵达后，我看见牌照号为 Settlement 16639 和 F. 1317 的两辆机动卡车停在美国领事馆大门外，周围有四名日本士兵，以及两名英国领事馆警卫列兵和一名警士。上午8时25分，一辆载有5名英国海军士兵的机动卡车经过外白渡桥并停下询问情况。随后决定被扣留的机动卡车应继续行程。日籍警员76号命令中国司机离开驾驶座，但该命令未被理会，机动卡车驶离，3名日本士兵在后追赶。
    片刻后，士兵们返回，为首的士兵抓住英国警卫指挥官的袖子，示意他随自己过外白渡桥，同时另有3名日本士兵从外白渡桥跑向英国领事馆。
    英国警卫指挥官从日本士兵手中抽回袖子，进入岗亭并按下警报铃，领事馆警卫的3名士兵立即端着刺刀出动，该警士装上刺刀，在领事馆大门前列队，并用步枪向日军士兵示意。日本人领会了警告，立即退至道路中央，双方交谈几句后，他们便向北经过外白渡桥离去。领事馆大门附近的行人道上其余日本平民也被清空。
                                        先生，您忠顺的仆人，
                                        R. 汤普森

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
North Soochow Road Station,
REPORT
Date. Oct, 30, 19 37.
Subject State of District.
Made by D.S.I. Kennedy Forwarded by Inspector
Officer in charge

Sir,
For the period ending 12 midnight 29-10-37. Police
operating from this Station arrested a total of 10 male Chinese
for petty looting and loitering with intent in the North Kiangse
Boone and Woochung Road Area. Property involved was of trivial
value, and the arrested persons were handed over to West Hongkew
Station to be dealt with.
At 7.10 a.m. 29-10-37, F.S.80 Williams telephoned the
Station to the effect that he had called the S.F.B. Ambulance to
Tuh Shing Li off North Kiangse Road to remove an injured person
to hospital. It was ascertained that said injured person, one
Ling Ah Ching, 23 years, S/Unemployed, native of Hangchow, had
entered this alleyway for the purpose of looting. He climbed on
to the roof of one of the houses where he was surprised by two
members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. He became frightened
and while trying to escape, fell from the roof sustaining injuries
which necessitated his removal to the Lester Chinese Hospital.
Doctor's chit states:- "Fracture of neck and Right femur" "Not
Serious" will require about 40 days treatment in hospital.
At about 2.45 p.m. 29-10-37 two armed pinnaces manned by
members of the J.N.L.Party were observed proceeding West along
the Soochow Creek.
D.C. (Divisions), Special Branch and D.O. "C" were
informed. British troops in charge of this area were rushed to the
scene and lined the banks of the Creek about 50 yards East of
Chekiang Road Bridge where the two pinnaces were compelled to stop
owing to the congestion of traffic. Negotiations were carried on
between G.U.C. British troops and Officers of the J.N.L.Party in
order that the pinnaces return, which they finally did at 5.10 p.m

档案号
北苏州路捕房，
报告
日期 1937年10月30日。
主题 辖区状况。
报告人 D.S.I. 肯尼迪 呈报人 主管巡官

先生，
截至1937年10月29日午夜12时的期间内，从本捕房出动的警察在北江西路宝兴路和吴淞路区域以轻微抢劫及意图游荡罪共逮捕了10名中国男子。涉案财产价值微薄，被捕人员已移交西虹口捕房处理。
1937年10月29日上午7时10分，F.S.80 威廉姆斯致电本捕房，称他已呼叫上海救火联合会救护车前往北江西路屠盛里，将一名伤者送往医院。经查，该伤者名为凌阿清，23岁，单身/无业，杭州人，进入该弄堂旨在行窃。他爬上一所房屋的屋顶，被两名日本海军陆战队队员发现。他受到惊吓，在试图逃跑时从屋顶坠落受伤，需送往莱斯中国医院治疗。医生证明写道：“颈部及右股骨骨折”“不严重”，需住院治疗约40天。
1937年10月29日下午2时45分左右，观察到两艘由日本海军陆战队队员驾驶的武装汽艇沿苏州河向西行驶。
已通知分区副总监、特别处及“C”区督察长。负责该区域的英军迅速赶赴现场，在浙江路桥以东约50码处的河岸列队，由于交通拥堵，两艘汽艇被迫停止。英国驻沪军队指挥官与日本海军陆战队军官之间进行了谈判，要求汽艇返回，最终它们于下午5时10分返回。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 30.10.37.

"Royal Welch Fusiliers
Turn Japanese Pinnaces
Back In Soochow Creek

STRONG VERBAL PROTEST MADE AGAINST
ENTRY OF CRAFT INTO "B" SECTOR;
BRIDGES MANNED BY TROOPS

COMPANY RUSHED TO POSTS ON DOUBLE
IN RESPONSE TO EMERGENCY CALL

Boats Held Up Within 700 Yards Of Chinese
"Death-With-Honour" Troops Holding Out
Grimly In Beleagured Godown

Doubling to their posts in response to an emergency call, a company of the Royal Welch Fusiliers yesterday afternoon manned North Chekiang Road and Yu Ya Ching Road Bridges over the Soochow Creek for more than an hour and a half while a strong verbal protest was being made by the British military authorities against the "invasion" of "B" sector by two Japanese naval craft.

Slim, blue-grey pinnaces armed with heavy machine-guns forward, the two craft lay in Soochow Creek about midway between North Chekiang Road Bridge and the small footbridge immediately to the east, strangely out of place among the thousands of junks and river craft crowded for safety into the narrow water-way, and still occupied by China's gypsies of the water.

Fewer than 700 yards west along the creek was the Continental Bank Godown made famous by the reckless heroism of a handful of Chinese soldiers holding the building against the Japanese Naval Landing Party. The scene was set perfectly for the midstream drama which took place as the vessels were called on to halt their passage through the channel. Overhead a slate, overcast sky; crowding the narrow lanes leading to the banks of the creek as close as Police cordons would permit them, hordes of sullen, half-scarred Chinese.

Intercepted by a British sentry's challenge, the two craft hove to in the narrow channel left open by the huddled, derelict riverboats, British military authorities, headed by Major-General A. P. O. Telfer-Smollett meanwhile racing down to the northern side of the Creek to meet hastily summoned Japanese naval and military officials.

High Officials Gather

Direct from the funeral of the Italian Grenadier at the Bubbling Well Road cemetery, General Telfer-Smollett immediately held a creekside conference, during which further Japanese officials were summoned to attend the discussion.

As General Telfer-Smollett conferred with the Japanese officials another party of foreign military authorities occupied positions of observation in the vicinity of Yu Ya Ching Road bridge. Among the observers were Colonel F. B. Price, commanding U.S. 4th Marines; Colonel F. R. W. Graham, commanding S.V.C., Lieutenant-Colonel L. Perretier, commanding French forces, Deputy-Commissioner Major K. M. Bourne, of the Settlement Police, and numerous staff officers.

"The Shanghai Times" understands that while the Japanese naval authorities explained that they had been requested to give escort upcreek to an S.M.C. fireboat, General Telfer-Smollett immediately entered a strong verbal protest against their entry into waters passing through the British Defence sector.

According to Japanese sources, the request for assistance to the fire float was made by Admiral Yarnell, a member of whose staff last night stated that the Admiral of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet had asked that the Japanese naval authorities permit the float to proceed up creek "without interference."

Homing Pigeons Released

As the discussions were taking place there was intense activity on board the two Japanese vessels. A wireless aerial was erected with two bamboo poles and after about three-quarters of an hour, a flight of homing pigeons was released.

While thousands waited tensely along the creek bank for further developments, units of the Russian Regiment proceeded to occupy sandbag redoubts facing Soochow Creek from the southern banks and police swiftly erected barbed wire barricades to force the crowds back along the streets.

It is understood that following General Telfer-Smollett's protest, the Japanese agreed to withdraw, and although offered an escort during their passage back down the creek they proceeded alone and safely back to their parent ship.

About 20 minutes before the two naval vessels appeared on the Creek, the S.M.C. fireboat passed through the two booms and proceeded up the creek to aid in fighting fires which were destroying mills at the western extension area. During the interval between the passage of the fireboat and the appearance of the two Japanese naval craft, however, the booms had been replaced and the one at the entrance to the creek had to be reopened to permit their entry.

Citadel Still Stands

For 90 minutes the creek incident had distracted the attention of large numbers of spectators, watching from every possible vantage point a grimmer drama which was being unfolded before them as a small group of Chinese soldiers stood the second day of a siege which has captured the imagination of many wherever the written word is read.

As the Japanese pinnace slowly backed down creek, however, a sharp crack from a field gun emplaced near the besieged godown again brought all eyes back to the building, over which waved significantly a huge Chinese flag, the "largest to be found in Shanghai."

How that flag reached the building has yet to be told, but in its appearance, it at least revealed that a means of direct communication with the troops had been found. When the flag was handed over to them during the night of Thursday the Chinese "Death-with-Honour" brigade also received a quantity of foodstuffs, it was ascertained by "The Shanghai Times" yesterday afternoon.

No official estimate of the number of men holding the post has been given by the Chinese authorities, but it is believed they are considerably fewer than the 500 at first estimated. The first official pronouncement of direct communication with the men was given yesterday at the Chinese Press Conference, when the official spokesman declared that he had met the commander of the post

"We Are Prepared"

"Our position is well-consolidated and we are well prepared for any emergency," the Commander declared.

A certain amount of relief was felt yesterday among those who had watched with sympathy the gallant stand of the troops when it was ascertained that a means of communication had been discovered. If there was a way in, there must be a way out, they reasoned.

From Chinese official sources, it was learnt yesterday that while a strong petition had been sent to Nanking requesting an order commanding the men to withdraw from the position, no reply had been received up till late yesterday.

That public sentiment was solidly against permitting the men to stay in the building until they were slaughtered was pointed out in the petition to Nanking, and Shanghai Chinese civic authorities meanwhile declared that they were unable to move individually in the matter, which was one of purely military affairs.

Defiant Stand

"Shed your last drop of blood in fulfilling your sacred duty of defending national territory for the glory of the Chinese race, the Chinese Republic and the Chinese Revolutionary Army. I and all my comrades salute you."

This is part of a message of encouragement sent yesterday by Lieutenant-General Sun Yuan-liang, Commander of the 88th Division, to the lone battalion at present still holding the two godowns of the Joint Savings and Trust Company on North Soochow Road in Chapei.

The gallantry and heroism embodied in their determination to die with Chapei, General Sun told them, had been highly praised by General Chiang Kai-shek, Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission.

"Though I have led my other men, in accordance with instructions, to a new defence line," General Sun said, "my spirit, my heart and my mind are with you in Chapei."

《上海泰晤士报》 - 1937年10月30日。

“皇家威尔士燧发枪团
在苏州河逼退日本炮艇

就船只进入‘B’区提出强烈口头抗议；
桥梁由部队驻守

响应紧急呼叫，连队跑步赶赴哨位

在距离中国‘誓死坚守’部队顽强据守的被围仓库700码内拦截船只

昨天下午，皇家威尔士燧发枪团的一个连响应紧急呼叫，跑步赶赴哨位，在苏州河上的浙江北路桥和虞洽卿路桥驻守了一个半小时。在此期间，英国军方当局对两艘日本海军炮艇‘入侵’‘B’区提出了强烈的口头抗议。

这两艘船艇瘦长，呈蓝灰色，前部装有重机枪，停泊在苏州河中，位于浙江北路桥与紧邻其东侧的小人行桥之间大约中点的位置。在为了安全而拥挤在这条狭窄水道中的成千上万只舢板和河船中间，它们显得格格不入，而这些水域仍由中国的水上吉普赛人占据着。

沿河道向西不到700码处，便是大陆银行仓库，因少数中国士兵不顾生死、英勇抵抗日本海军陆战队而在此据守而闻名。当被要求停止穿越航道时，一场发生在河中央的戏剧性场面完美地展开了。头顶是石板色的阴沉天空；成群面色阴郁、身上带有半旧伤痕的中国人，挤在通往河岸的狭窄巷弄里，尽量靠近警察警戒线允许的范围。

两艘船艇在英国哨兵的喝令下被截停，在由聚集在一起的废弃河船留出的狭窄通道中抛锚停船。与此同时，以A. P. O. Telfer-Smollett少将为首的英国军方当局迅速赶往苏州河北岸，去会见被紧急召来的日本海陆军官员。

高级官员聚集

Telfer-Smollett将军刚从静安寺路公墓参加完意大利掷弹兵的葬礼回来，立即在河边举行会议，期间又召集了更多日本官员参加讨论。

当Telfer-Smollett将军与日本官员会谈时，另一批外国军事当局人员在虞洽卿路桥附近占据了观察位置。观察者中包括美国海军陆战队第4团团长F. B. Price上校、上海志愿军（S.V.C.）指挥官F. R. W. Graham上校、法军指挥官L. Perretier中校、工部局警务处副总巡官K. M. Bourne少校，以及众多参谋军官。

据《上海泰晤士报》获悉，虽然日本海军当局解释说他们是应请求为工部局的一艘消防艇提供护航溯流而上，但Telfer-Smollett将军立即对其进入流经英方防区的海域提出了强烈的口头抗议。

据日方消息来源称，对消防船的援助请求是由Yarnell上将提出的，其幕僚中的一员昨晚表示，美国亚洲舰队司令已要求日本海军当局允许该消防船‘不受干扰地’溯流而上。

释放信鸽

在讨论进行时，两艘日本舰艇上活动频繁。用两根竹竿架起了无线天线，大约过了三刻钟后，放飞了一群信鸽。

当成千上万的人在河岸边紧张地等待事态进一步发展时，俄国团的部队开始占领南岸面向苏州河的沙袋堡垒，警察迅速架设铁丝网路障，迫使人群沿街道后退。

据悉，在Telfer-Smollett将军提出抗议后，日本人同意撤离，尽管在他们顺流返回途中有人提出为其护航，但他们还是独自安全地回到了母舰。

在两艘海军舰艇出现在苏州河上之前约20分钟，工部局的消防船穿过了两道拦河坝，溯流而上，协助扑灭正在摧毁西区延伸地带工厂的大火。然而，在消防船通过与两艘日本海军舰艇出现之间的这段时间里，拦河坝已被重新放置，因此不得不重新打开入口处的拦河坝以允许其进入。

孤堡依然屹立

苏州河事件在90分钟内吸引了大量观众的注意力，他们从每一个可能的有利位置观看着一场更为严峻的戏剧在他们面前展开：一小群中国士兵正处于围困的第二天，这场围困已经抓住了所有阅读文字报道的人的想象力。

然而，当日本炮艇缓缓倒退出河道时，在被围仓库附近部署的一门野战炮发出的一声尖锐巨响，再次将所有的目光引回了那座建筑，上面飘扬着一面巨大的中国国旗，意味深长，号称‘上海最大’。

这面旗帜是如何到达建筑物的尚待讲述，但它的出现至少表明，已经找到了与部队直接联系的方法。《上海泰晤士报》昨天下午获悉，当这面旗帜在周四夜间移交给他们时，中国‘誓死坚守’旅还收到了一批食品。

中国当局尚未官方估计据守该阵地的人数，但据信远少于最初估计的500人。昨天在中国新闻发布会上首次正式宣布与该部队取得了直接联系，当时官方发言人宣称他会见了该阵地的指挥官

“我们已做好准备”

“我们的阵地已得到巩固，我们为任何紧急情况做好了充分准备，”指挥官宣称。

昨天，那些曾同情地注视着部队英勇坚守的人们，在得知已发现通讯手段后，感到了一定程度的宽慰。他们的推理是，既然有路进去，就一定有路出来。

昨天从中国官方消息来源获悉，虽然已向南京发送了一份强有力的请愿书，请求下令命令该部队从阵地撤离，但直到昨天深夜仍未收到回复。

向南京提交的请愿书中指出，公众舆论坚决反对让士兵留在建筑物中直至被屠杀，与此同时，上海中国市政当局声明，他们无法就此事单独采取行动，因为这纯属军事事务。

蔑视性的坚守

“为了中华民族、中华民国和中国革命军的荣耀，履行保卫国土的神圣职责，流尽最后一滴血。我和我所有的同志向你们致敬。”

这是第88师师长孙元良中将昨天发给目前仍在闸北苏州北路坚守四行信托部两个仓库的孤立营的鼓励电文的一部分。

孙将军告诉他们，他们那种与闸北共存亡的决心所体现的勇敢和英雄气概，受到了军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军的高度赞扬。

孙将军说：“虽然我已遵照指示率领其他部下撤至新的防线，但我的精神、我的心和我的思想与你们同在闸北。”

page_data.en:
Chinese Dig In
Chinese troops yesterday morning
began to dig in east of Keswick Road
near the Western perimeter, while
a light field gun was placed west of
Brenan Road railway crossing, toge-
ther with a machine-gun emplace-
ment. Four attempts by Chinese
soldiers to finish the demolition of
Jessfield Railway Bridge were re-
ported in the early hours of the
morning, but a girder was still span-
ning the two ends last night.
During the course of the after-
noon, the British troops along the
boundary were witnesses to great
aerial activity as Japanese planes
machine-gunned the nearby Chinese
positions and dropped several bombs,
one of which landed in Edinburgh
Road near Brenan Road during the
late afternoon.
One objective of the Japanese
aerial raiders was the newly-prepar-
ed Chinese machine-gun posts about
every 100 yards along the railway
line.
Official Visits
Developments attracted much in-
terest from both naval and military
authorities, some of whom visited
the British post near the Jessfield
Bridge during the day.
A check-up with the French au-
thorities at a late hour last night
revealed the fact that all was quiet
again along the boundary line of the
Concession.
It was generally felt here that if a
dangerous situation developed along
the Concession boundary the French
would take strong action in accord-
ance with the attitude they have
maintained here since the opening
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities with
regard to the protection of lives and
property.
Threat To Nantao
"Although still preparing to attack
Chinese positions on the southern
bank of Soochow Creek, the Japan-
ese army authorities are also con-
sidering possible action against
Chinese troops that fled into Nan-
tao," a spokesman for the Japanese
military declared yesterday after-
noon.
"There is evidence," the spokes-
man said, "that a large number of
Chinese troops are in Nantao."
"Due precautions," the spokesman
asserted, "will be taken to safeguard
establishments in the French Con-
cession."
page_data.zh:
中国军队挖掘工事
昨天上午，中国军队开始在西部外围附近的凯斯威克路（Keswick Road）以东挖掘工事，同时在布伦南路（Brenan Road）铁路道口以西部署了一门轻型野战炮以及一个机枪阵地。据报道，清晨时分中国士兵四次试图完成杰斯菲尔德铁路桥的爆破工作，但昨晚仍有一根大梁横跨两端。
下午期间，边界沿线的英军目睹了大规模的空中活动，日本飞机对中国军队附近的阵地进行机枪扫射并投下数枚炸弹，其中一枚在傍晚时分落在布伦南路附近的爱丁堡路（Edinburgh Road）。
日本空袭者的目标之一是沿铁路线每隔约100码新设的中国机枪阵地。
官方访问
事态发展引起了海陆军当局的高度关注，其中一些人在白天参观了杰斯菲尔德桥附近的英军哨位。
昨晚深夜与法国当局核实后发现，租界边界沿线再次恢复平静。
这里普遍认为，如果租界边界沿线出现危险局势，法国人将根据自中日敌对行动开始以来他们在保护生命和财产方面所保持的态度，采取强硬行动。
对南市的威胁
“虽然日军当局仍在准备攻击苏州河南岸的中国军队阵地，但他们也在考虑对逃入南市的中国军队采取可能的行动，”一位日本军方发言人昨天下午宣称。
“有证据表明，”该发言人说，“南市有大量中国军队。”
该发言人断言：“将采取适当的预防措施，以保护法租界内的机构。”

page_data.en:
CHINA PRESS - 30.10.37.

British Stop
Nippon Unit
Sailing Creek

Clash Averted By Timely
Intervention Of High
Officers

SAMPANS PLACED
ACROSS STREAM

Move Directed At Big
Godown Defended By
Chinese Battalion

British troops with fixed bayonets stopped a Japanese Navy landing party from going up Soochow Creek past Chekiang Road Bridge to get at the "suicide battalion" of Chinese soldiers in a godown at Yu Ya Ching Road yesterday afternoon. A solid mass of junks brought quickly together by Chinese laodahs just above the bridge blocked the passage and aided the soldiers in stemming the invasion. No shots were fired by either the British or Japanese forces.

The action taken by the British military was not a desire to stem an attack on the godown but was executed because Japanese apparently were using that section of Soochow Creek traversing the International Settlement as a means of gaining a position in front of the beleaguered Chinese troops.

The Japanese marines, filling two naval launches, proceeded up the creek from the Whangpoo at 2:30 p.m. and were halted by "C" Company of the Royal Welch Fusiliers when they were about to pass under Chekiang Road bridge.

Traffic Held Up 3 Hours

For two hours and 15 minutes the British and Japanese forces faced each other as the former patrolled the bank of the creek and the bridge while the latter stood by in the stream below.

The Fusiliers who thwarted the Japanese attempt to pass through their sector were quartered in the godown of the Bank of China, on the north bank of the creek, across Thibet Road from where the so-called "doomed battalion" of Chinese soldiers have been holding off Japanese attacks for three days.

As soon as the Japanese boats, holding between 30 and 40 men, approached the Chekiang Road bridge, the British contingent hastened out with bayonets fixed on their rifles and took up extended order positions along North Soochow Road and the span.

Colonel Marchard, commander of the Royal Welch Fusiliers who are defending the sector, approached the bank of Soochow Creek and informed the Japanese officer in charge of the expedition in no uncertain terms that they were in the British defense zone without permission. The Japanese squatted in their launches, completely surrounded by sampans and junks which had by this time formed a complete circle around them until the arrival of Brigadier-General A.P.D. Telfer-Smolett with Captain Fujita, liaison officer of the Japanese navy. Following brief negotiations, the two launches withdrew rapidly downstream.

The Fusiliers were matched back to billets, and the hundreds of pedestrians and vehicles swarmed across the bridges to make up for lost time. Police had cordoned off Chekiang Road, a block from the bridge, and all other spans to the east had also been closed.

Meanwhile Settlement Police were busy holding back traffic on both sides of the creek, so that no civilians would be injured, in the event of an armed clash. Fortunately, negotiations between the British and Japanese authorities were settled amicably, and at about 4.45 p.m. the two boatloads of Japanese departed in the direction from which they came.

Traffic was resumed with scenes similar to an evacuation, as the crush of people swept across five bridges from both ends. Whether the Japanese boats would have been able to reach their objective, irrespective of the Settlement defense force interference, is problematical in view of the jam of Chinese non-combatant craft just above Chekiang Road Bridge. From that point on to Yu Ya Ching Road Bridge the channel is very narrow, and yesterday afternoon it appeared to be blocked with junks.

Throughout the incident, the atmosphere was tense. Lowering clouds and the threat of a storm did not lessen the feeling that "something was going to happen." Over the godown of the Joint Savings Society around the bend the Chinese ensign fluttered briskly in the breeze.

Japanese Explain More

The explanation that the Japanese gave for their little excursion up Soochow Creek was that they had been requested by the American authorities to escort a municipal fire float up the stream.

The fire float, they said, was going upstream to fight a blaze in an American godown on the Chapel side of the creek and since the Japanese are now in occupation of that sector, they were asked to escort the float.

American authorities, when questioned, knew nothing about such an arrangement. It was learned, however, that a fire float did proceed up the creek during the day but seven hours in advance of the "escort"!

Launches Well Armed

The float, THE CHINA PRESS was informed, was sent up the creek to dampen down ruins in Chapel along the edge of the stream. It was used instead of Fire Brigade trucks for reasons of economy. It takes its supply of water from the creek and not from the municipal hydrants.

Examination of the two launches used by the Japanese revealed that in addition to the 30 or more men on board each one, they were protected with armored plate while each carried a three-pound gun as well as a machine-gun.

During the conversations between British officers and the Japanese, the latter declared that they were under orders from their commander to proceed upstream and before withdrawing, desired to notify him. The launches were not equipped with wireless but the Japanese had come prepared. They released five carrier pigeons.

Lone Unit Carries On

In the meantime, the Chinese battalion under its valiant commander, Colonel Hsieh Chin-yuan, continued last night to hold out against the best that the Japanese have been able to offer thus far.

The Chinese flag purchased for them by the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce appeared on top of the building yesterday morning as scheduled. It was the largest flag in all Chapel No Rising Sun banner in the whole of the area could approach it in size.

To obtain the flag, Chinese officials searched the city most of Thursday night. The fact that it was successfully got through to the beleaguered soldiers astounded Shanghai yesterday morning. Crowds of curious gathered at all possible points of vantage and found it fluttering over the Joint Savings Society godown as advertised.

Food Smuggled Through

The appearance of the flag also gave credence to the story circulated yesterday morning that a truck-load of food was successfully negotiated through to the men during the night by three Chinese Boy Scouts.

Fighting around the godown yesterday was of a sanguinary nature. The Japanese still continued to machine-gun the place and as near as could be ascertained, causing no damage, and no casualties. It was reported last night that the Japanese had moved a battery of fieldpieces to the west of the godown with the apparent idea of shelling the place. Foreign military observers, however, point out that even at close range, this will be more or less futile since, if the Japanese want to hit the godown, which is located between other buildings, it will take days of blasting. If they over-shoot, shells will land in the Settlement. If they attempt to blast it out with aerial bombs, one poorly aimed missile will most likely land in the Settlement.

《字林西报》 - 1937年10月30日。

英军阻止
日军部队
溯苏州河而上

高级军官及时干预
避免冲突

舢板横亘
河道之中

行动旨在针对
由中国营队防守的
大型仓库

昨日下午，英军士兵装上刺刀，阻止日本海军登陆队沿苏州河驶过浙江路桥，去攻击位于余姚路一处仓库内的中国士兵“敢死队”。由中国船老大迅速集结在桥上方的一群密集的帆船和驳船封锁了通道，协助士兵遏制了入侵。英日双方均未开枪。

英军采取的行动并非意在阻止对仓库的攻击，而是因为日本人显然正利用穿越公共租界的那段苏州河，作为在被围困的中国军队前方占据阵地的手段。

下午2时30分，两艘满载海军陆战队员的日本汽艇从黄浦江驶入苏州河向上游进发，在即将通过浙江路桥下时，被皇家威尔士燧发枪团（Royal Welch Fusiliers）C连拦阻。

交通中断三小时

在两个多小时的时间里，英日双方对峙，前者在河岸和桥上巡逻，后者则在下游的水面上待命。

挫败日军试图穿过其防区的燧发枪团驻扎在苏州河北岸的中国银行仓库内，隔着西藏北路，与所谓“注定牺牲”的中国士兵营队相望，后者已在此抵挡日军进攻三天。

当日军载有30至40人的船只靠近浙江路桥时，英军分队迅速出动，步枪装上刺刀，沿北苏州路和桥梁展开散兵线部署。

负责防守该区域的皇家威尔士燧发枪团指挥官马查德上校（Colonel Marchard）走近苏州河畔，毫不含糊地告知带队日军军官，他们未经许可进入了英军防御区。日军蹲坐在汽艇中，此时已被舢板和帆船完全包围，这些船只已在他们周围形成一个完整的圆圈，直到特尔弗-斯莫利特准将（Brigadier-General A.P.D. Telfer-Smolett）与日本海军联络官藤田大尉（Captain Fujita）抵达。经过简短谈判，两艘汽艇迅速向下游撤退。

燧发枪团士兵返回营房，数百名行人和车辆涌过桥梁，以弥补失去的时间。警察已封锁距桥头一个街区的浙江路，其他所有向东的桥梁也已关闭。

与此同时，租界巡捕忙于在河道两岸控制交通，以防万一发生武装冲突时平民受伤。幸运的是，英日当局之间的谈判和平解决，下午4时45分左右，两船日军沿来路撤离。

交通恢复时的景象类似于疏散，人群从两端涌过五座桥梁。鉴于浙江路桥上方挤满了中国非战斗人员的船只，无论租界防卫部队是否干预，日军船只能否到达目标都是个问题。从那里到余姚路桥，河道非常狭窄，昨天下午似乎被帆船堵塞。

在整个事件过程中，气氛紧张。低垂的乌云和风暴的威胁并未减轻人们“即将发生什么事”的感觉。转过弯处的四行储蓄会仓库上空，中国国旗在微风中 briskly 飘扬。

日方进一步解释

日军对其溯苏州河而上的小小远征给出的解释是，他们应美国当局请求，护送一艘市政消防趸船沿河而上。

他们说，消防趸船逆流而上是为了扑灭河道小教堂（Chapel）一侧一家美国仓库的火灾，由于日军目前占领了该区域，因此被要求护送该趸船。

美国当局在被问及此事时，对此类安排一无所知。然而获悉，确实有一艘消防趸船在当天沿河而上，但比“护航”早了七个小时！

汽艇武装精良

据《字林西报》获悉，派遣趸船沿河而上是为了浇湿小教堂沿河岸边的废墟。出于节约原因，使用趸船而非消防车。它从河中取水，而非从市政消防栓取水。

对日军使用的两艘汽艇的检查显示，除了每艘船上30多名人员外，它们还装有装甲板，并且每艘都携带一门三磅炮以及一挺机枪。

在英日军官交谈期间，后者宣称他们奉指挥官命令向上游进发，并在撤退前希望通知指挥官。汽艇未配备无线电，但日军已做好准备。他们释放了五只信鸽。

孤军奋战

与此同时，在中国英勇指挥官谢晋元上校（Colonel Hsieh Chin-yuan）率领下的中国营队，昨晚继续坚守，抵挡日军迄今为止所能投入的最强兵力。

由中国总商会为他们购买的五星红旗于昨天上午按计划出现在楼顶。这是整个小教堂地区最大的一面旗帜。该地区任何一面旭日旗在尺寸上都无法与之相比。

为了获得这面旗帜，中国官员在周四夜间的大部分时间里搜遍全城。旗帜成功送达被围困士兵手中的事实，昨天早晨令上海震惊。好奇的人群聚集在所有可能的有利位置，发现正如宣传的那样，旗帜在四行储蓄会仓库上空飘扬。

食物走私进入

旗帜的出现也证实了昨天早晨流传的说法，即三名中国童子军在夜间成功将一卡车食物运送给守军。

昨天仓库周围的战斗性质血腥。日军继续用机枪扫射该处，据尽可能查明，未造成损坏或伤亡。昨晚据报道，日军已将一组野战炮移至仓库西侧，明显意图炮击该处。然而，外国军事观察家指出，即使在近距离，这也或多或少是徒劳的，因为如果日军想击中位于其他建筑物之间的仓库，需要数天的爆破。如果炮弹射偏，将落在租界内。如果他们试图用航空炸弹将其炸毁，一枚瞄准不佳的导弹极有可能落入租界。

SHANGHAI TIMES - 30.10.37.

CREEK INCIDENT BEING SETTLED

The "Soochow Creek Incident" yesterday afternoon, involving Japanese naval and British military authorities, is seen being settled above. The commander of the two Japanese pinnaces, which proceeded up the creek, is seen jotting down some notes, while another Japanese officer, who acted as interpreter, looks on. Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett, who requested the Japanese to return, is seen at the extreme right.
[World News Photo.

Protest Lodged
By Japanese

Action on the part of members of the British Defence Force stationed at North Thibet Road Bridge on Soochow Creek in "boarding a Japanese naval launch escorting a Municipal fire float up the Creek" last night drew a protest from the Japanese Naval Authorities, Domei reported.

《上海泰晤士报》 - 1937年10月30日。

河道事件正在解决

昨日下午涉及日本海军和英国军事当局的“苏州河事件”如上所示正在得到解决。图中可见溯河而上的两艘日本尖头艇指挥官正在 jotting down 一些笔记，另一名担任翻译的日本军官在一旁观看。要求日军返回的特尔弗-斯莫利特少将（Major-General A. P. D. Telfer-Smollett）位于最右侧。
[世界新闻照片。

日方提出抗议

据同盟社报道，昨晚驻扎在苏州河北西藏路桥的英国防卫部队成员“登上一艘护送市政消防趸船溯河而上的日本海军汽艇”的行动，引起了日本海军当局的抗议。

G. COM 137
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Fil. No. 117/37.
Gordon Road
REPORT
October 29, 37.
Subject Situation in Gordon Road District.
Made by D.S.I.Cumming, & Forwarded by Inspector i/c.
Sir,
A Chinese female named ung Siau Ong Ts(陳小英)
mentioned in my daily report of 27/10/37,as having been injured
by shrapnel succumbed to her injuries at 2.30 p.m. 28/10/37
in the St.Elizabeth's Hospital. An inquest is being held.
During the afternoon of 28/10/37,Japanese
combatants on duty in the Chapel Area East of the Soochow
Creek prepared a raft with the intention of crossing to No.9
Mill situated at Markham Road & Soochow Road corner for
supplies. Major Skinner(U.S.M.C.) refused to allow this
procedure and the matter was explained through an interpreter
to the employers of the mill in question.
At about 11.20 p.m. 28/10/37,one Koo Siau Sen Ts
(□ □),male,3 years,Kompo,straw hut off Changping Road
near Gordon Road,was struck by an anti-aircraft missile
whilst sleeping. The child was removed to St.Elizabeth's
Hospital where a Dr.'s certificate was issued,reading as
follows:- Laceration right hand.Fracture of carpal bone".
Regarding the mill situation,the Ying On Cotton
Mill 381 Markham Road,resumed night operation again 28/10/37.
D. S. I.
D.D.O."B" Division.
Copy forwarded to C.D.I.Ross,Sp.Br.

G. COM 137
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 117/37。
戈登路
报告
1937年10月29日。
主题：戈登路地区局势。
由副督察卡明（D.S.I. Cumming）撰写，并由主管督察转发。
先生，
我在1937年10月27日的日报中提到的名为陈小英（ung Siau Ong Ts(陳小英)）的中国女性，因弹片受伤，于1937年10月28日下午2时30分在圣伊丽莎白医院伤重不治。目前正在举行死因研讯。
1937年10月28日下午，在苏州河以东小教堂区域执勤的日本战斗人员准备了一只筏子，意图渡河前往位于马克姆路（Markham Road）与苏州路拐角处的第九棉纺厂获取补给。斯金纳少校（Major Skinner，美国海军陆战队）拒绝允许此程序，并通过翻译向该厂雇主解释了此事。
1937年10月28日晚上11时20分左右，一名名叫顾小森（Koo Siau Sen Ts (□ □)）的男童，3岁，籍贯广东，住在戈登路附近昌平路旁的草棚内，在睡觉时被防空导弹击中。该儿童被送往圣伊丽莎白医院，医生出具的证明如下：“右手撕裂伤。腕骨骨折”。
关于工厂情况，位于马克姆路381号的永安棉纺厂于1937年10月28日恢复夜间作业。
副督察
B区副分区助理局长。
副本 forwarded to 特别处罗斯首席督察（C.D.I. Ross, Sp.Br.）。

G. 20/1-37
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8039/30
Gordon Road Station, No 37
Date October 28, 19 37%
Subject Situation in Gordon Road District.
Made by D.S.I.Cumming, & Forwarded by Inspector i/c, White.

Sir,
At 1.30 p.m. 27/10/37, a Japanese soldier swam over the
Soochow Creek at Markham and Soochow Road junction for the
purpose of connecting a hose from the Chapel side to a hydrant
in No.9 Mill(Japanese). The connection was made but the mem-
bers of the U.S.M.C.on duty there cut the hose and threw it
back into the creek. J.P.S.127 and three other Japanese, one
of whom was in military uniform were in the vicinity, and on
instructions by Colonel Cates they were taken to the U.S.M.C.
Headquarters Intelligence Dept.These persons were informed that
in case of complications arising no assistance of this nature
would be rendered to the Japanese forces.

During an air-raid at 1.30 a.m. 28/10/37, shrapnel
fell on Gordon Road outside the Station Gate. No injuries or
damage.

The Wing On Cotton Mill and Hung Chang Cotton Mill,
491 & 381 Markham Road respectively, ceased night operation
on 27/10/37 owing to the fire in Chapei.

（左侧批注：The water supply is now connected by arrangement between the military authorities concerned ld.）
（左侧印章：RECEIVED 28 OCT 1937）
（左侧批注：Seen Jnt 29/10）

S/Q Cumming
D.S.I.
D.D.O. "B" Div. 29/10
Copy sent to C.E. I. Roux, Sp. Asst. C 29/10

G. 20/1-37
上海公共租界工部局警务处
报告
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别处登记处
编号 S. B. D. 8039/30
戈登路站，第37号
日期 1937年10月28日
主题：戈登路地区局势。
由副督察卡明（D.S.I. Cumming）撰写，并由主管督察怀特（White）转发。

先生，
1937年10月27日下午1时30分，一名日本士兵在马克姆路与苏州路交汇处游过苏州河，目的是将软管从小教堂一侧连接到第九棉纺厂（日资）的消防栓。连接已完成，但在那里执勤的美国海军陆战队成员切断了软管并将其扔回河中。日本警员127号（J.P.S.127）和其他三名日本人（其中一人身穿军装）在附近，根据凯茨上校（Colonel Cates）的指示，他们被带到美国海军陆战队总部情报部。这些人被告知，如果出现并发症，将不会向日军提供此类援助。

1937年10月28日凌晨1时30分的空袭期间，弹片落在站门外戈登路上。无人员伤亡或财产损失。

位于马克姆路491号和381号的永安棉纺厂和鸿章棉纺厂，因闸北火灾，于1937年10月27日停止夜间作业。

（左侧批注：供水现在已通过有关军事当局之间的安排连接。）
（左侧印章：1937年10月28日 收讫）
（左侧批注：Jnt 阅 1937年10月29日）

S/Q 卡明
副督察
B区副分区助理局长 10月29日

An urgent emergenay conference, 
under the auspices of Japanese residents interested in the U.S. 
Marine incident, was held at the Tairiku Hall on Seward Road at 
8 peme July 10 in response to the indignation expressed by the 
70,000 Japanese residents in Shanghai and their demand for the 
chastisement of the Fourth American Marine Corps which had paid 
no heed to the atrocious action which had harmed the dignity 
and prestige of the Japanese Imperial Army. 16 persous 
delivered addresses to an audience of about 3,000, impeaching 
the American Marines and spurring on the Japanese authorities. 

After issuing a declaration and 
passing a resolution, the conference came to a close at 10 p.m.

are as follows :- 

The assault committed on our 
gendarmes by the American Marines is an outrage, an exceedingly 
grave insult; it is a frank expression of America's hostility 
towards Japan. It is not at all like an unexpected accident 
of a trivial nature. The dignity of the Imperial Army has been 
completely harmed. The prestige of our Imperial Government has 
been trampled on with muddy feet. The blood shed by 100,000 
loyal soldiers would have been shed in vain. We, the subjects 
of the great Imperial Japanese Government, will never overlook 
the issue. Should Amerioa attempt to temporize, the relations 
between Japan and America may become endangered. 

It is a clear fact that America 
is an old enemy of those who are rebuilding Asia. The 
indignation of our nation has reached its climax and our 
forbearance has a limit. Furthermore, America is attempting 
to obstruct the activities of our Imperial Government in every 
field in the place of all third Powers whioh are hostile to 
Japan. In order to attain the object of our holy war we should 
order all anti-Japanese Powers, including America, which are 
supporting Chiang Kai-shek, to withrraw from the Far East and 
we will contime to make every uffost until we succeed in 
removing completely the influence of these Powers. 

We shall maintain a striot watch 


over the developments in this incident. This is our declaration.
